claims.text: This charge is not a first occurrence between these two parties, and that is the fact a single-trip view cannot reach. EV-TRIP-02755 records rider RDR-09755 and driver DRV-09755 — the two parties described by the profile artifacts — and both profiles' own trailing-90-day counters for disputes with a counterparty read 2: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2. The rider's filing describes this as the third time this same driver has cancelled on her and charged her. POL-NS-09(c) is drafted to read those two fields together and to send the case to a human reviewer where they show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver; read with POL-GEN-01, which permits those two fields to be cited for precisely this test and no other, the limb is satisfied on the counters themselves.

Escalation is the only outcome available on this record that takes the disputed $4.50 out of collection. POL-NS-09 makes escalation terminal and places the disputed cancellation fee on hold rather than collected or refunded while review is pending, and POL-GEN-03 provides that an ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and replaces the ruling. The ledger confirms where the money sits now: EV-FARE-02755 shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged SGD 4.50 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so if the case is not escalated this fee simply stands as charged.

The arrival on this trip is a driver-pressed marker, not a platform-confirmed one: EV-TRIP-02755 carries arrival_marker BUTTON together with its wait-timer events, so POL-NS-12 — which lets platform arrival and wait-timer telemetry stand in for the export only where the marker is GPS_AUTO — does not apply, and the charge must stand on the exported trace's own POL-NS-02 proximity test. The bundle's one third-party artifact, EV-ADVIS-02755-01, is MISSING, carrying issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0: it is disclosed here as carrying no fact and corroborating nothing, and its absence is itself the record that no advisory covers Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 in this window.

The rider's own device track is not a condition of this charge and cannot be used to make the charge good. POL-NS-01 decides the fee on the driver's arrival, dwell and termination code, and POL-NS-06 answers the shortfall question whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages; nothing in this category makes the rider's proximity to the pickup pin a ground for collecting the fee. The rider_track figures in EV-GPS-02755 (70 fixes, no qualifying fix inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius) therefore do not support a charge that the driver's own arrival and dwell evidence does not itself establish.

The rider does not ask the tribunal to find the cancellation premature: the export's derived arrival block records one continuous in-geofence run of 390 seconds at this STANDARD pickup, longer than the 180-second free waiting period the record's own platform_policy carries, and the rider puts no shortfall case under POL-NS-06. What the record does not settle — and what no single-trip arithmetic in this file decides — is whether a third cancellation-and-charge between this same rider and driver should be adjudicated as though it stood alone. That question is the one POL-NS-09(c) sends to a human reviewer, and it is where the rider's case rests.

The trip record carries the platform's own driver 'arrived' event for this trip: at 09:14:14 the driver tapped 'I'm Here' on TRP-02755, which is limb (a) of the baseline chargeable no-show test satisfied on telemetry rather than on assertion.

Arrival is independently established by GPS, not by the button: the trace holds 40 qualifying fixes inside the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m, and the first of them is timestamped 09:14:14 — the very same second as the arrival event — so the driver was inside the pickup geofence at (and before the end of) the marker event, satisfying limb (b) of POL-NS-01 under the POL-NS-02 proximity test. The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (10 s cadence, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0).

The dwell is long and continuous: the longest qualifying in-geofence run runs from 09:14:14 to 09:20:44, a continuous 390 seconds across 40 fixes. That is 210 seconds more than the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180, with no longer no_show_threshold_sec set), and it clears the 300-second STANDARD figure in the fee schedule as well, so limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied with room to spare.

The termination matches the no-show reason code exactly: no boarding event appears anywhere in the record and the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:20:47 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — 3 minutes 33 seconds after the required 180-second dwell elapsed at 09:17:14 — which is limb (d) of POL-NS-01 on its face.

The arrival marker is a button tap and so is exposed to the false-arrival test, and it survives it: the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at the marker's own timestamp (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), his track minimum distance is 0.0 m, and the stationary fixes sit inside the 50 m radius rather than more than 300 m out or at 15 km/h or above. There is therefore no false marker, the waiting clock needs no recomputation, and the fee is not defeated under POL-NS-05.

There is no waiting-period shortfall to refund: measured against the minimum in force the shortfall figure is negative — shortfall_sec -210.0 on a 390-second qualifying run against the 180-second STANDARD minimum — so the refund route in POL-NS-06 never opens. Because a single continuous in-geofence interval already exceeds the minimum, the interval-accumulation route in limb (i) is not needed either.

The driver does not rest anything on the traffic advisory, and says so: EV-ADVIS-02755-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and because the dwell is already sufficient on a single in-geofence interval the driver neither needs nor asserts limb (i) of POL-NS-06. Nothing in the driver's case depends on that absent artifact.

The wrong-entrance clause cannot rescue the rider here, because its premise is absent: POL-NS-03 applies only where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, whereas on this trace 40 qualifying fixes lie INSIDE the 50 m radius from 09:14:14 onward. The driver was at the pickup point, not at a wrong face of it.

The rider-contact clause cannot exonerate the rider either, on either required limb: the chat log's single message is the DRIVER'S 'im here', sent 09:14:44 and read 09:15:14, with no locating or coordinating message from the rider at all, so limb (a) fails; and the rider's own track holds zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, sitting 847.65 m to 855.43 m from the pin across all 70 fixes, so limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes rather than undecidable. Both the chat artifact and the GPS trace are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the chat log's 1 message matches trip_record.chat_message_count of 1, so there is no POL-NS-08(c) defect.

No grace provision protects this cancellation: it was made at 09:20:47, some 14 minutes after accepted_at 09:06:49, far outside the 180-second grace_after_match_sec, and the trip was not a scheduled trip (scheduled_at is null) so no advance-scheduled window applies. The non-chargeability routes in POL-NS-10(a) and (b) are therefore unavailable on this record.

The ledger is internally sound and matches the fee in force: cancellation_fee and total_charged are both 4.50, exactly platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd for this trip, with no waiting-time line charged and every ledger line reconciling, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare-integrity defect that would force the amount down. payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the fee in force — 0.80 x 4.50 = 3.60 SGD — and the anti-farming check does not trip, because driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below the 4 required) and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 110 is 0.018 (below the 0.08 rate). Both limbs of the check must hold and neither does, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

The rider's assertion of a repeated pattern is a party statement, not a finding: under POL-GEN-01 profile data may not establish a fact about this trip or carry an adverse finding, and the only profile counters in issue on the driver's side — no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d, for the POL-NS-07 test — show no farming pattern. The deciding facts here rest on complete, weight-1.0 artifacts: the in-geofence dwell and the recorded reason code.

ruling.explanation: To both parties. The trip mechanics themselves are not in dispute, and on them the driver is right. DRV-09755 tapped 'arrived' at 09:14:14 (EV-TRIP-02755), and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02755, weight 1.0, COMPLETE, 10-second cadence, no gaps) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that same second, with 40 qualifying fixes. He then held position continuously for 390 seconds — against the 180-second free waiting period this trip's own platform_policy carries — and terminated at 09:20:47 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, more than three minutes after the required dwell had elapsed. That satisfies all four limbs of POL-NS-01 (arrival event, GPS proximity, dwell, reason code and timing). POL-NS-05 does not bite: the first qualifying fix is at the marker's own timestamp, the driver was stationary at the pin (min distance 0 m) and never at speed on the arrival timestamp, so the marker is genuine and the waiting clock needs no recomputation. POL-NS-06 gives no refund — the shortfall is negative, 390 s against 180 s, recorded as -210 s. POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-04 do not apply: the driver was inside the radius, not at a wrong face of the venue, and the only chat message is the driver's own 'im here' with no locating message from the rider, so POL-NS-04 limb (a) fails (its limb (c) also fails on the rider's track, which shows no qualifying fix within 100 m). POL-NS-10's grace windows are long past (cancellation about 14 minutes after acceptance, on an unscheduled trip). The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02755) reconciles to the $4.50 fee in force, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect, and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. EV-ADVIS-02755-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it carries no fact and nothing here rests on it. Standing alone, this would be a verified rider no-show and POL-NS-07 would pay the driver 80% of $4.50 = $3.60, the anti-farming check not tripping (no_show_terminations_30d = 2, below 4; 2/110 = 0.018, below 0.08). But the case does not stand alone. POL-NS-09(c) sends a case to human review where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. Both read 2 (EV-RPROF-02755 and EV-DPROF-02755, each at weight 1.0) for this same pair, RDR-09755 and DRV-09755 on TRP-02755, and the rider's filing describes this as the third such cancellation and charge. That trigger is aimed at repeat behaviour a single-trip view cannot fairly assess, and it fires. I reject the driver's contrary argument (made under POL-GEN-01) insofar as it says the profile counters can never support an escalation: POL-GEN-01 expressly lists disputes_with_counterparty_90d on both profiles as citable for this test; what it excludes is the lifetime counters (prior_no_show_flags) and the rider's bare assertion of a 'pattern', neither of which I have used. Because POL-NS-09 escalation is terminal and, per POL-GEN-03, replaces the ruling, no money moves now: the $4.50 disputed cancellation fee is placed on hold — not collected and not refunded — and the driver's compensation is not paid pending review. This is not a finding for either side. The question for the reviewer is whether the repeated rider/driver history (2 recorded counterparty disputes in 90 days, with the rider alleging a third) warrants anything different from the verified single-trip outcome, and the case summary goes to that reviewer with both briefs, the admissibility report, the clauses relied on and this reasoning. No referral clause fires: POL-NS-05's false-arrival record is not engaged (the marker was genuine) and POL-NS-07's anti-farming branch does not trip. Confidence is 0.90: the escalation rests on two independent weight-1.0 profile artifacts, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0, above the 0.70 floor; and the amount is held in any event.

To both parties: this case goes to a human reviewer and no money moves now. On the merits the driver's account is accepted. EV-TRIP-02755 shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:14:14 on TRP-02755; EV-GPS-02755 places him inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius from that same second, with 40 qualifying fixes and one continuous in-geofence run of 390 seconds ending 09:20:44; the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:20:47 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (platform_policy.free_wait_sec; no longer no_show_threshold_sec is set) and 390 seconds clears it, so limbs (a) to (d) of POL-NS-01 all hold, the $4.50 cancellation fee on EV-FARE-02755 would stand, and POL-NS-07 would fix the payout at 80% of it, $3.60, because the anti-farming check does not trip: 2 no-show terminations in 30 days is below the 4 required, and 2 divided by 110 completed trips is 0.018, below the 0.08 rate. The rider's defences are answered and rejected. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate her: the only chat message is the driver's own 'im here', so limb (a) fails, and her device track sits 848 to 855 m from the pin across all 70 fixes, so limb (c) fails affirmatively rather than being undecidable. POL-NS-03 does not apply, because the stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius rather than at a wrong face of the venue. POL-NS-05 does not catch the arrival marker: the trace corroborates it at its own timestamp, not more than 300 m away and not at 15 km/h or above. POL-NS-06 opens no refund, since there is no shortfall. POL-NS-10 gives no grace: the cancellation came about 14 minutes after match, far outside the 180-second grace_after_match_sec, and the trip was not scheduled. The missing advisory EV-ADVIS-02755-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is disclosed and carries no fact, and POL-NS-12 is inapplicable because the arrival marker is BUTTON, though the exported trace supports the arrival independently in any event. The case is nevertheless escalated under POL-NS-09(c): rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d each read 2, that is two no-show disputes between this same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days, consistent with the rider's own account that this is the third such cancellation. Both profile artifacts are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. POL-GEN-01 permits exactly these two fields to be cited for this test, so the driver's objection that profile data cannot ground a finding is rejected as applied to POL-NS-09(c): the counters prove nothing about this trip and are used only to open the repeat-conduct review. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal under POL-GEN-03 and replaces any monetary ruling, so the otherwise-payable $3.60 driver compensation is not paid and the $4.50 fee is neither collected nor refunded but held. No clause produces a referral: POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival record does not fire because the marker is not false, and POL-NS-07's anti-farming packet instruction does not fire because the check does not trip. The open question the reviewer must settle is whether the two prior disputes between this rider and driver disclose abuse or fee-farming on either side that a single-trip view cannot fairly assess, and, on the merits recorded above, whether the $4.50 charge should stand with $3.60 to the driver or be disposed of otherwise. The monetary effect in play ($3.60 to $4.50) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00, but nothing is executed while review is pending.

To both parties: the SGD 4.50 no-show fee on TRP-02755 is HELD — not refunded to the rider and not paid over to the driver — and this case goes to a human reviewer under POL-NS-09(c). No money moves now and no compensation issues at this stage.

WHY THE CASE ESCALATES. POL-NS-09(c) sends a case to human review where the rider's and the driver's trailing-90-day counts of disputes with a counterparty together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver. On this record both counts read 2: EV-RPROF-02755.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 for rider RDR-09755 and EV-DPROF-02755.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 for driver DRV-09755 — the same two parties as on this trip — so the clause's '2 or more' threshold is met. POL-GEN-01 permits these two fields, and only these two, to be cited, and only for this test, so the rider's use of them is proper; the rider's own statement that this is 'the third time this same driver has cancelled on me and charged me' is a party account and is not itself the ground, but the structured counters independently satisfy the limb. POL-NS-09 makes escalation terminal and POL-GEN-03 makes it replace the ruling.

THE DRIVER'S MERITS CASE — ACCEPTED BUT DISPLACED. I accept the driver's POL-NS-01 case in full: (a) EV-TRIP-02755 carries the driver's own 'arrived' event at 09:14:14; (b) EV-GPS-02755 places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that same second, with 40 qualifying in-geofence fixes; (c) he held position continuously in-geofence for 390 s, from 09:14:14 to 09:20:44, against the 180 s free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is null); and (d) the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:20:47 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event. I also accept that the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05 (the first qualifying fix carries the marker's own timestamp, dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0, inside the radius and stationary), that POL-NS-06 discloses no shortfall (390 s − 180 s = 210 s of surplus; derived shortfall_sec −210.0), that POL-NS-03 is not engaged because the stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius rather than merely within 400 m of the pin, that POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider (the chat log's only message is the driver's 'im here', so limb (a) fails; the rider track shows no qualifying fix within the 100 m presence radius, sitting 847.65 m to 855.43 m from the pin), that POL-NS-10's grace routes do not apply (cancellation some 14 minutes after accepted_at 09:06:49, and scheduled_at is null), and that the ledger is sound (cancellation_fee and total_charged both SGD 4.50, matching the fee in force, with no waiting-time line, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect).

Had the case stood alone, those findings would have produced DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.60 under POL-NS-07 (80 percent of SGD 4.50), the anti-farming check not tripping (no_show_terminations_30d = 2, below the required 4; 2 ÷ 110 = 0.018, below 0.08). Because POL-NS-09(c) fires, that monetary outcome does not issue now. No displaced clause directs an instruction into the packet: the POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival referral is not engaged (the marker is genuine) and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming refund direction is not engaged either, so the referrals list is empty.

THE OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER. Whether the repeated no-show disputes between this same rider and driver — 2 within the last 90 days on both counters, plus the rider's account of a third — indicate a pattern of repeat conduct between this pair that a single-trip view cannot fairly assess in either direction, and, if so, how the SGD 4.50 fee and any driver compensation should be allocated.

EVIDENCE NOTE. The only artifact below full weight is EV-ADVIS-02755-01, a MISSING traffic advisory at weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. It carries no fact, nobody relies on it, and the driver's dwell is sufficient on a single in-geofence interval so POL-NS-06(i) is not needed; its absence is not a ground in this ruling. Every artifact that carries the deciding fact — the two profile counters, read with the trip and GPS records — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap on this ruling's confidence is 1.0.

Dispatch: the disputed SGD 4.50 is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded, and the escalation packet carries both briefs, the admissibility report, the clauses relied on and this reasoning.

POL-NS-09 makes escalation terminal and POL-GEN-03 makes it replace the ruling.

THE DRIVER'S MERITS CASE — ACCEPTED BUT DISPLACED. I accept the driver's POL-NS-01 case in full: (a) EV-TRIP-02755 carries the driver's own 'arrived' event at 09:14:14; (b) EV-GPS-02755 places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that same second, with 40 qualifying in-geofence fixes; (c) he held position continuously in-geofence for 390 s, from 09:14:14 to 09:20:44, against the 180 s free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is null); and (d) the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:20:47 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event. I also accept that the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05 (the first qualifying fix carries the marker's own timestamp, dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0, inside the radius and stationary), that POL-NS-06 discloses no shortfall (390 s − 180 s = 210 s of surplus; derived shortfall_sec −210.0), that POL-NS-03 is not engaged because the stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius rather than merely within 400 m of the pin, that POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider (the chat log's only message is the driver's 'im here', so limb (a) fails; the rider track shows no qualifying fix within the 100 m presence radius, sitting 847.65 m to 855.43 m from the pin), that POL-NS-10's grace routes do not apply (cancellation some 14 minutes after accepted_at 09:06:49, and scheduled_at is null), and that the ledger is sound (cancellation_fee and total_charged both SGD 4.50, matching the fee in force, with no waiting-time line, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect).

Had the case stood alone, those findings would have produced DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.60 under POL-NS-07 (80 percent of SGD 4.50), the anti-farming check not tripping (no_show_terminations_30d = 2, below the required 4; 2 ÷ 110 = 0.018, below 0.08). Because POL-NS-09(c) fires, that monetary outcome does not issue now. No displaced clause directs an instruction into the packet: the POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival referral is not engaged (the marker is genuine) and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming refund direction is not engaged either, so the referrals list is empty.

THE OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER. Whether the repeated no-show disputes between this same rider and driver — 2 within the last 90 days on both counters, plus the rider's account of a third — indicate a pattern of repeat conduct between this pair that a single-trip view cannot fairly assess in either direction, and, if so, how the SGD 4.50 fee and any driver compensation should be allocated.

EVIDENCE NOTE. The only artifact below full weight is EV-ADVIS-02755-01, a MISSING traffic advisory at weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. It carries no fact, nobody relies on it, and the driver's dwell is sufficient on a single in-geofence interval so POL-NS-06(i) is not needed; its absence is not a ground in this ruling. Every artifact that carries the deciding fact — the two profile counters, read with the trip and GPS records — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap on this ruling's confidence is 1.0.

Dispatch: the disputed SGD 4.50 is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded, and the escalation packet carries both briefs, the admissibility report, the clauses relied on and this reasoning."

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: here is where the case landed and why.

On the merits, the $4.50 charge is supported by the record. EV-TRIP-02755 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) carries the driver's own 'arrived' event at 09:14:14, and EV-GPS-02755 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0; 90 fixes at 10 s cadence, 100.0% coverage, max gap 0.0 s) independently puts him inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius from that same second — 40 qualifying in-geofence fixes, the first at 09:14:14 — so POL-NS-01 limb (b) holds under the POL-NS-02 proximity test. He then held position continuously for 390 seconds (09:14:14 to 09:20:44) against the 180-second free waiting period in force (free_wait_sec 180; no longer no_show_threshold_sec is set), and the trip was terminated at 09:20:47 under RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event anywhere in the record — limbs (c) and (d) hold with 210 seconds to spare. The button arrival marker is genuine (dwell start offset 0.0 s, minimum distance 0.0 m, no 300 m or 15 km/h breach at the marker), so POL-NS-05 does not fire; there is no shortfall under POL-NS-06 (shortfall_sec -210.0); the driver's stationary fixes are inside the radius rather than at a wrong face of the building, so POL-NS-03 does not apply; and the rider sent no locating or coordinating message (the chat log's only message is the driver's 'im here', 09:14:44) while her device sat 847.65–855.43 m from the pin across all 70 rider fixes, so POL-NS-04 does not exonerate her. The ledger reconciles: cancellation_fee and total_charged are both 4.50, matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. On that basis POL-NS-07 would have paid the driver 80% of SGD 4.50, i.e. SGD 3.60, and the charge would have stood.

The case does not end there. POL-NS-09(c) sends a case to human review where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. Both counters read 2 (EV-RPROF-02755 and EV-DPROF-02755, both COMPLETE at weight 1.0), on exactly the rider and driver on this trip. POL-GEN-01 expressly permits those two fields to be cited for that test and no other, so the driver's POL-GEN-01 objection does not meet the limb: the limb does not use the profiles to prove anything about this trip, it asks the platform to look at a pattern a single-trip view cannot see. The rider's escalation ground is accepted. The rider advocate's claims are accepted, and the driver advocate's findings on limbs (a)–(d), POL-NS-05, POL-NS-06, POL-NS-03, POL-NS-04, POL-NS-08(d) and POL-NS-07 are accepted as findings on the merits — but they cannot produce a money ruling, because escalation is terminal.

ESCALATE replaces the ruling under POL-GEN-03: no monetary outcome issues, and the disputed SGD 4.50 is held rather than collected or refunded while review is pending. EV-FARE-02755 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) shows the fee is presently collected; this ruling neither confirms nor reverses it. POL-NS-07's anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d = 2, below the 4 required; 2 / 110 completed trips = 0.018, below the 0.08 rate), so no instruction to refund the rider is written into the review packet and no compensation figure is fixed. No clause produces a referral on these facts: the arrival marker was not false, so POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire; POL-NS-03 does not apply, so its obligations do not fire; and the fare and driving records are clean.

Disclosure of impaired material: EV-ADVIS-02755-01 (traffic advisory) is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. It carries no fact, it makes POL-NS-06(i) unavailable, and neither side relies on it, so it does not affect the outcome. Every other artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the decision rests on facts carried by those weight-1.0 artifacts, so confidence is 0.90.

Open question for the human reviewer: whether the trailing-90-day record between RDR-09755 and DRV-09755 — 2 disputes recorded on each side, with the rider alleging this is the third time the same driver has cancelled on her and charged her — shows a repeat no-show pattern warranting action against either party, and whether the SGD 4.50 charge stands once that pattern is assessed.

ledger.claim: This charge is not a first occurrence between these two parties, and that is the fact a single-trip view cannot reach. EV-TRIP-02755 records rider RDR-09755 and driver DRV-09755 — the two parties described by the profile artifacts — and both profiles' own trailing-90-day counters for disputes with a counterparty read 2: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2. The rider's filing describes this as the third time this same driver has cancelled on her and charged her. POL-NS-09(c) is drafted to read those two fields together and to send the case to a human reviewer where they show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver; read with POL-GEN-01, which permits those two fields to be cited for precisely this test and no other, the limb is satisfied on the counters themselves.

Escalation is the only outcome available on this record that takes the disputed $4.50 out of collection. POL-NS-09 makes escalation terminal and places the disputed cancellation fee on hold rather than collected or refunded while review is pending, and POL-GEN-03 provides that an ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and replaces the ruling. The ledger confirms where the money sits now: EV-FARE-02755 shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged SGD 4.50 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so if the case is not escalated this fee simply stands as charged.

The arrival on this trip is a driver-pressed marker, not a platform-confirmed one: EV-TRIP-02755 carries arrival_marker BUTTON together with its wait-timer events, so POL-NS-12 — which lets platform arrival and wait-timer telemetry stand in for the export only where the marker is GPS_AUTO — does not apply, and the charge must stand on the exported trace's own POL-NS-02 proximity test. The bundle's one third-party artifact, EV-ADVIS-02755-01, is MISSING, carrying issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0: it is disclosed here as carrying no fact and corroborating nothing, and its absence is itself the record that no advisory covers Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 in this window.

The rider's own device track is not a condition of this charge and cannot be used to make the charge good. POL-NS-01 decides the fee on the driver's arrival, dwell and termination code, and POL-NS-06 answers the shortfall question whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages; nothing in this category makes the rider's proximity to the pickup pin a ground for collecting the fee. The rider_track figures in EV-GPS-02755 (70 fixes, no qualifying fix inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius) therefore do not support a charge that the driver's own arrival and dwell evidence does not itself establish.

The rider does not ask the tribunal to find the cancellation premature: the export's derived arrival block records one continuous in-geofence run of 390 seconds at this STANDARD pickup, longer than the 180-second free waiting period the record's own platform_policy carries, and the rider puts no shortfall case under POL-NS-06. What the record does not settle — and what no single-trip arithmetic in this file decides — is whether a third cancellation-and-charge between this same rider and driver should be adjudicated as though it stood alone. That question is the one POL-NS-09(c) sends to a human reviewer, and it is where the rider's case rests.

The trip record carries the platform's own driver 'arrived' event for this trip: at 09:14:14 the driver tapped 'I'm Here' on TRP-02755, which is limb (a) of the baseline chargeable no-show test satisfied on telemetry rather than on assertion.

Arrival is independently established by GPS, not by the button: the trace holds 40 qualifying fixes inside the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m, and the first of them is timestamped 09:14:14 — the very same second as the arrival event — so the driver was inside the pickup geofence at (and before the end of) the marker event, satisfying limb (b) of POL-NS-01 under the POL-NS-02 proximity test. The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (10 s cadence, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0).

The dwell is long and continuous: the longest qualifying in-geofence run runs from 09:14:14 to 09:20:44, a continuous 390 seconds across 40 fixes. That is 210 seconds more than the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180, with no longer no_show_threshold_sec set), and it clears the 300-second STANDARD figure in the fee schedule as well, so limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied with room to spare.

The termination matches the no-show reason code exactly: no boarding event appears anywhere in the record and the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:20:47 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — 3 minutes 33 seconds after the required 180-second dwell elapsed at 09:17:14 — which is limb (d) of POL-NS-01 on its face.

The arrival marker is a button tap and so is exposed to the false-arrival test, and it survives it: the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at the marker's own timestamp (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), his track minimum distance is 0.0 m, and the stationary fixes sit inside the 50 m radius rather than more than 300 m out or at 15 km/h or above. There is therefore no false marker, the waiting clock needs no recomputation, and the fee is not defeated under POL-NS-05.

There is no waiting-period shortfall to refund: measured against the minimum in force the shortfall figure is negative — shortfall_sec -210.0 on a 390-second qualifying run against the 180-second STANDARD minimum — so the refund route in POL-NS-06 never opens. Because a single continuous in-geofence interval already exceeds the minimum, the interval-accumulation route in limb (i) is not needed either.

The driver does not rest anything on the traffic advisory, and says so: EV-ADVIS-02755-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and because the dwell is already sufficient on a single in-geofence interval the driver neither needs nor asserts limb (i) of POL-NS-06. Nothing in the driver's case depends on that absent artifact.

The wrong-entrance clause cannot rescue the rider here, because its premise is absent: POL-NS-03 applies only where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, whereas on this trace 40 qualifying fixes lie INSIDE the 50 m radius from 09:14:14 onward. The driver was at the pickup point, not at a wrong face of it.

The rider-contact clause cannot exonerate the rider either, on either required limb: the chat log's single message is the DRIVER'S 'im here', sent 09:14:44 and read 09:15:14, with no locating or coordinating message from the rider at all, so limb (a) fails; and the rider's own track holds zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, sitting 847.65 m to 855.43 m from the pin across all 70 fixes, so limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes rather than undecidable. Both the chat artifact and the GPS trace are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the chat log's 1 message matches trip_record.chat_message_count of 1, so there is no POL-NS-08(c) defect.

No grace provision protects this cancellation: it was made at 09:20:47, some 14 minutes after accepted_at 09:06:49, far outside the 180-second grace_after_match_sec, and the trip was not a scheduled trip (scheduled_at is null) so no advance-scheduled window applies. The non-chargeability routes in POL-NS-10(a) and (b) are therefore unavailable on this record.

The ledger is internally sound and matches the fee in force: cancellation_fee and total_charged are both 4.50, exactly platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd for this trip, with no waiting-time line charged and every ledger line reconciling, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare-integrity defect that would force the amount down. payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the fee in force — 0.80 x 4.50 = 3.60 SGD — and the anti-farming check does not trip, because driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below the 4 required) and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 110 is 0.018 (below the 0.08 rate). Both limbs of the check must hold and neither does, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

The rider's assertion of a repeated pattern is a party statement, not a finding: under POL-GEN-01 profile data may not establish a fact about this trip or carry an adverse finding, and the only profile counters in issue on the driver's side — no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d, for the POL-NS-07 test — show no farming pattern. The deciding facts here rest on complete, weight-1.0 artifacts: the in-geofence dwell and the recorded reason code.
